dog.description_text:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Spike is at risk due to behavioral reasons. In his previous home Spike was observed to be reactive to the resident dog. He would lunge and snap at the resident dog and snap at whoever would pull him away from the dog. It was stated that Spike had poor impulse control and would jump up on strangers while barking at them. In the care center, Spike has engaged well with dogs during playgroup with a loose and wiggly body. He greets staff with soft body, enjoys time in the yard, and rest his body on staff for pets. Spike is known to be reactive to dogs in the kennel but has been non-reactive to dogs or people on walks. Medically, Spike is healthy at this time.

Spike has been reported to display some concerning behaviors at the care centers, he has been reported to display a tense body and be fearful with some staff and his former home have reported he is reactive to dogs and will snap/lunge toward them as well as whomever handles him and pulls him away from dogs. We recommend placement with a New Hope rescue partner who is able to provide an experienced, adult-only foster home. Force-free, reward based training and/or consultation with a professional trainer/behaviorist is highly recommended.
